# authwise_realm_authentication_policy (Resource)

A realm's authentication policy: the rules, the floor, enrollment, remembered devices, session, throttle, risk and the acr levels (`RealmConfig.authentication`).

It is managed apart from `authwise_realm` so the two do not fight over the realm's config: the realm resource never reads or writes this part of it, and does not accept an `authentication` key in its own `config`. The policy is authoritative — it replaces whatever policy the realm had — and destroying it clears the policy, leaving the realm on kit's defaults.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `realm` (String) Full resource name of the realm the policy governs (`tenants/{t}/realms/{r}`), e.g. `authwise_realm.x.name`. Changing it moves the policy: the old realm's is cleared and the new realm's is written.

### Optional

- `acr_levels` (Attributes List) The acr vocabulary this realm can emit, weakest first: the last satisfied entry is the emitted acr. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--acr_levels))
- `enrollment` (Attributes) Setting this block at all switches kit from its defaults to the values here, `in_flow` included: kit reads an absent enrollment policy as in-flow enrollment on, and a present one at face value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--enrollment))
- `floor` (Attributes) The least any rule may require: every outcome is raised to it, so a misjudged rule can only ask for more. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--floor))
- `remember_device` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--remember_device))
- `risk` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--risk))
- `rules` (Attributes List) Rules, evaluated in order; the first whose condition holds decides. A realm with no rules behaves as one rule `true` requiring the floor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `session` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--session))
- `throttle` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--throttle))

<a id="nestedatt--acr_levels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `acr_levels`

Optional:

- `name` (String)
- `require` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--acr_levels--require))

<a id="nestedatt--acr_levels--require"></a>
### Nested Schema for `acr_levels.require`

Optional:

- `allowed_factor_types` (List of String) Factor types that may count. Empty means every factor enabled on the realm.
- `deny_reason` (String) Mode `DENY` only. Recorded in the audit trail, never shown to the person.
- `hardware_bound` (Boolean) With `PHISHING_RESISTANT`: the authenticator must not be backup-eligible.
- `min_factors` (Number) Distinct factor classes required beyond the primary's own. 0 means the mode's default, which for `ANY_FACTOR` is 1.
- `mode` (String) What must hold beyond the primary: `NONE`, `ANY_FACTOR`, `TYPES`, `PHISHING_RESISTANT` or `DENY` (never valid as the floor).
- `reauth_after` (String) A factor verified longer ago than this does not count. Unset falls back to `session.factor_reauth`. A Go duration string, e.g. `90s`, `15m`, `12h`.
- `required_factor_types` (List of String) Factor types that must all be present (mode `TYPES`).
- `skip_if_device_trusted` (Boolean) Whether a trusted device satisfies the requirement without a factor. Never honoured for `PHISHING_RESISTANT` or `DENY`.



<a id="nestedatt--enrollment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `enrollment`

Optional:

- `grace` (String) A Go duration string, e.g. `90s`, `15m`, `12h`.
- `in_flow` (Boolean) Whether a person may enrol a factor inside the login flow when a rule demands one they lack.
- `offer_recovery_codes` (Boolean) Whether recovery codes are offered after the first factor is enrolled.
- `self_service_types` (List of String) Factor types a person may add from the account page. Empty means every factor enabled on the realm.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Optional:

- `condition` (String) CEL over the authentication context. Empty or `true` always matches. kit checks it on write, so a bad expression fails the apply with kit's reason.
- `name` (String) The rule's name, recorded on the login event. kit refuses an unnamed rule.
- `require` (Attributes) What the rule requires; raised to the floor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--require))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by full resource name.
# The realm's full resource name: the policy is part of the realm.
terraform import authwise_realm_authentication_policy.example tenants/t-01/realms/r-01
```
